title: Colorado Skier Miraculously Survives Avalanche - NewsBreak
text:
By Nate Wilde ,
8 hours ago
Backcountry skiing can be a fun, high-adrenaline activity, but it can also be highly dangerous. This was made evident recently as a man who was skiing on Colorado’s Berthoud Pass not only triggered an avalanche while doing so, but miraculously survived the ordeal.
Man Survives Avalanche on Colorado’s Berthoud Pass On Sunday, January 18, between 2 and 3 p.m., a man who has yet to be identified publicly was backcountry skiing on Colorado’s Berthoud Pass, an area high in the Colorado Rockies along the Continental Divide. The man and an unnamed companion were skiing on a run known as “Postage Stamp” when he is said to have triggered an avalanche.
Download the KKNN Mobile App Now Once the avalanche was triggered, the man was carried by the rushing snow an estimated 200 yards down the mountain, and once the avalanche stopped at the base of the peak, he found himself buried up to his waist in snow.
Numerous people witnessed the avalanche and the man being swept up by it and notified authorities. Luckily, the man was able to free himself before search and rescue even arrived on the scene.
The man has spoken to news outlets about the ordeal, stating that he was fully aware that the area was prone to avalanches and that the particular section of the mountain that he chose to ski was especially dangerous, but he chose to ski that section of Berthoud Pass anyway.
The Colorado Avalanche Information Center has reported that the parts of Berthoud Pass that are most prone to avalanches are sections of the mountain that face east, south, and southeast, which is where the avalanche was triggered.
Not only did the man survive the avalanche that he triggered, but he also walked away uninjured.

The Development of Colorado's Ski Industry A lot of events had to take place for Colorado to become the world-class skiing destination that it is today. Gallery Credit: Nate Wilde Canva Mailmen on Skis Skiing first started to become popular in Colorado before it was even a state as it was the only way for mail to be delivered to miners back in the 1860s. Canva Steamboat and Crested Butte Catch the Skiing Bug Colorado mountain towns such as Steamboat Springs and Crested Butte saw skiing become very popular among residents in the late 1800s and early 1900s. Canva Winter Carnival held in Hot Sulfur Springs A winter carnival was held in 1911 in Hot Sulfur Springs which introduced skiing to a massive amount of people. Canva Howelsen Hill Established The birth of Howelsen Hill was a monumental event in the history of Colorado's ski industry. Canva National Ski Tournament in America A huge ski tournament held in Genessee in 1921 introduced the sport to the masses in a big way. Canva Berthoud Pass Brings Skiers The opening of Berthoud Pass inspired skiers to hit the slopes alongside the road which saw the sport quickly gain popularity. Canva First Ski Lodge is Opened The first ski lodge was built from old military barracks by the U.S. Forest Service in the 1930s. Canva First Tow Rope Before chairlifts, Denver's The May Company financed the first tow rope in the late 1930s. Canva Roche Run Established Long before Aspen was a major ski resort, locals built Roche Run on the side of Ajax Mountain. Canva First Ski Lift is Built The first ski lift in Colorado was built at Gunnison's Cement Creek ski hill in 1939. Canva Monarch Mountain Opens Monarch Mountain became Colorado's first official ski area in 1939. Winter Park Opens Winter Park was considered Colorado's first major ski area and first opened in 1940. Canva Birth of 10th Mountain Division The 10th Mountain Division was immensely responsible for the Colorado ski industry and was founded at Camp Hale between 1941 and 1942. Canva Huge Growth Colorado saw a huge influx of skiers and development of ski areas across the state between 1945 and 1947. Canva Vail and Snowmass Founded After WWII, 10th Mountain Division veterans founded the ski areas of Vail and Snowmass. Canva Vail Opens 1962 was a huge year for the Colorado ski industry as it saw the opening of Vail. Canva No Olympics for Beaver Creek Coloradans decided that they didn't want the 1976 Winter Olympics to be held at Beaver Creek. Canva First Snowboarding Competition The first-ever snowboarding competition was held at Colorado's Ski Cooper near Leadville in 1981. Canva Vail Resorts Founded In 1987, Vail Resorts was established as a conglomeration of resorts such as Vail, Breckenridge, Keystone and Arapahoe Basin. Canva World Snowboarding Championships The World Snowboarding Championships were first held at Breckenridge Ski Resort in 1990. Canva Snowboarding Joins the Olympics 1998 was a pivotal year for the sport of snowboarding, thanks in part to its popularity in Colorado.
